§6EEPROM & BIOS§f

§aThe tiny chip that tells your computer how to wake up.§f
Every OC computer needs an EEPROM to boot. The default Lua BIOS looks for a disk drive with an operating system on it.

§6Size Limits§f:
The EEPROM holds §e4096 bytes§f of executable code and §e256 bytes§f of configuration data. That's it. Don't try to write your OS to it.

§6Custom BIOS§f:
Use a Blank EEPROM in an EEPROM Writer to flash custom boot code. Writing costs §e50 energy§f, which is deliberately expensive to discourage constant rewrites.

§9Boot Order§f:
If you have multiple drives, use §bcomputer.setBootAddress(address)§f in the Lua shell to pick which one to boot from.

§ePS:§f OpenComputers runs Lua 5.3 by default. Your BIOS code must conform to the Lua API.
